criteria.text: The participant has a pathologically (histologically or cytologically) proven diagnosis of non-operable stage IIB or III, node positive (American Joint Committee on Cancer [AJCC] eighth edition) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with known PD-L1 status prior to registration

source.text: Patients must have an identified primary tumor and at least one nodal metastasis (peribronchial/hilar/intrapulmonary, mediastinal/subcarinal, supraclavicular/scalene)

criteria.text: The participant has received up to 4 cycles of systemic therapy prior to registration for the current study cancer, and any prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is permissible

criteria.text: The participant refuses surgery, or is technically unresectable, or is medically inoperable

source.text: Patients who refuse surgery, in addition to those who are technically unresectable or medically inoperable, are eligible.

criteria.text: The participant has separate tumor nodules in the same lobe of the primary tumor

criteria.text: The participant is deemed clinically appropriate for curative intent definitive combined modality therapy

source.text: The patient must be deemed clinically appropriate for curative intent definitive combined modality therapy, based on the following staging assessments:

criteria.text: A history and physical examination is performed prior to registration

source.text: History/physical examination prior to registration;

criteria.text: An MRI scan of the brain (preferred) or CT scan of the brain (if available, contrast is preferred for all neuroimaging) is performed prior to registration

source.text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan of the brain (preferred) or CT scan of the brain (if available, contrast is preferred for all neuroimaging) prior to registration;

criteria.text: A CT chest with IV contrast (if contrast is available and unless contraindicated, such as for abnormal kidney function) is performed prior to registration. PET/CT may be used if the CT portion is of identical diagnostic quality as achieved in a stand-alone CT

criteria.text: There is no evidence of distant metastases based on an FDG PET/CT scan obtained within 60 days of registration

criteria.text: If a pleural effusion is present, criteria must be met to exclude malignant involvement

source.text: If a pleural effusion is present, the following criteria must be met to exclude malignant involvement:

source.text: When pleural fluid is visible on both the CT scan and on a chest x-ray, a pleuracentesis is required to confirm that the pleural fluid is cytologically negative;

criteria.text: Effusions that are minimal (i.e., not visible on chest x-ray) that are too small to safely tap are eligible

criteria.text: The participant does not have an identifiable primary tumor and at least 1 pathologically enlarged lymph node (T3-4N0 or T0N1-3 patients are not eligible). At least 1 radiographically-involved lymph node is required, but pathologic confirmation of involvement is not mandated

source.text: Patients without identifiable primary tumor and at least 1 pathologically enlarged lymph node are not eligible (T3-4N0 or T0N1-3 patients are not eligible). At least 1 radiographically-involved lymph node is required, but pathologic confirmation of involvement is not mandated

criteria.text: The participant has a centrally located primary tumor < 2 cm from involved nodal disease that would result in significant overlap of the primary SBRT and nodal radiation fields. This does not include proximity to involved segmental and subsegmental lymph nodes (levels 13 and 14) that would not result in overlap of dose to the proximal bronchial tree or esophagus. Centrally located is defined as within or touching the zone of the proximal bronchial tree, which is a volume 2 cm in all directions around the proximal bronchial tree (carina, right and left main bronchi, right and left upper lobe bronchi, intermedius bronchus, right middle lobe bronchus, lingular bronchus right and left lower lobe bronchi)
